chunks: Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man to whom a woman had authorized her affairs, or a near relative of hers, or a neighbor of hers, who did not know of the hidden matter of her affairs, so he was found to have concealed a defect that was in her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The dower is taken from her, and there is nothing upon the one who married her off.'

key_terms.دَخِيلَةَ أَمْرِهَا: The hidden or interior matter/condition of her affairs

ai.seo_question: What happens to the dower if a marriage proxy concealed a defect in the woman?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial liability in marriages arranged by proxies (*wakil*) who act in good faith; if a hidden defect (*dajas*) is discovered, the proxy recovers the dower but incurs no penalty, emphasizing the principle of *ghabn* (deception) rather than contractual invalidity. This highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the validity of the contract and the restitution of rights when material conditions are misrepresented by the party or their agent.

en.hubeali: Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Dawood Bin Sirhan, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from IBn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby altogether,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man to whom a woman had authorised her command, or a near relative of hers, of a neighbour of her who did not know of the interior matter, so he was found to have cheated over a fault which was with her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The dower would be taken from her, and there would not be anything upon the one who got her married off’.
en.sarwar: 10. Sahl has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud ibn Sarhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy all who have said the following:

About the case of a man who is appointed by a woman to manage her affairs or a relative or a neighbor who does not know about her cheating and he finds her as cheating about a defect which exists in her. He (the Imam) said, ‘She must pay back the mahr (dower) and the one who has given her in marriage does not owe anything.’”
